title.narrative: Output 4.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop policies, legislation and other measures that are specifically aimed at facilitating the transition of enterprises to formality

description.narrative: The Association of Lebanese Industrialists (ALI) has established a help desk as a new service to informal enterprises in the agrifood sector to facilitate their transition to formality, through awareness raising on the benefits of formalization and preparation for adaption of the Formalize Your Business (FYB) set of training tools to the Lebanese context. 20 beneficiaries of a business plan competition received a grant and been coached to develop their business through Productive Sectors Development Programme (PSDP) funded by the Lebanon Recovery Fund through the generous contribution from the Government of Canada and implemented by UNIDO, FAO, UNDP, ILO, UNWOMEN, and UNICEF with support from the RCO in overall coordination. Through co-funding from the EU, the ILO "Social Dialogue for Formalization and Employability in the Southern Neighbourhood Region" (SOLIFEM) , in cooperation with ACT/EMP and the Enterprise Department, has established an Implementation Agreement with ALI for the purposes of supporting the employer organization to offer this new service on formalization to informal economic units after their transition to formality with the technical support of ALI and its network of experienced enterprises, will be able join the organization as members. This work involves the adaptation and roll out of the Formalize Your Business (FYB) Training to the Lebanese context. The ILO has also provided the resources for the recruitment of a consultant to lead the establishment of the help desk and the services and outreach to informal enterprises in the agrifood sector. This builds on the "Review of relevant registration, compliance procedures and institutional actors for the formalization of small economic units and their workers in Lebanon" done in 2022 under the PROSPECTS project to support the organization the agriculture and agro-food sector. Under the PSDP joint-UN framework the ILO conducted a progressive training cycle, starting with 218 MSMEs and entrepreneurs who received Women do Business training, followed by an advanced “business resilience” workshop with: •108 selected beneficiaries who presented a business plan at the end of their participation for evaluation and selection for the business plan competition event.102 beneficiaries succeeded in submitting a feasibility study and 40 was selected to take part in the “Women Do Business Experience” competition in order to demonstrate the acquired skills in a real life and business-oriented theme. 20 beneficiaries were announced as winners of a business plan competition and received a grant and business development coaching led by implementing partner the LEE Experience.
